name: On-demand marketplace matching & pricing (healthcare staffing, delivery, freight, mobility)
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases - current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: On-demand marketplace matching and dynamic pricing - real-time per-supplier (clinician / driver / dasher / courier / carrier / contractor) reliability features, per-(skill, zone, time) demand-supply features, per-customer / per-facility reliability features that drive (a) supplier-to-request matching, (b) ranked offer / batch construction, and (c) dynamic charge-rate / bill-rate / surge / spot-rate decisions on every request, offer, accept / decline, complete and cancel event in healthcare staffing, on-demand delivery, freight brokerage and ride / micromobility marketplaces
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A matching / pricing service in an on-demand marketplace (healthcare per-diem shifts, delivery, freight load, ride request) decides on every shift-post / order-create / load-tender / ride-request - within tens to hundreds of ms on the inline matching path and seconds on the dynamic-pricing path - which suppliers to surface or assign and what charge / bill / spot rate to quote, by reading per-supplier rolling acceptance / fill / cancellation / on-time / no-show features, per-(skill x zone x time) demand-supply counters, and per-customer / per-facility / per-shipper reliability features.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Power the per-supplier reliability score (per-clinician fill rate, per-driver acceptance rate, per-carrier first-tender-acceptance rate, per-dasher completion rate) over rolling 7/30/100-offer or 30-day windows so the matcher can rank suppliers beyond raw distance + price - this is the Uber 'last-100-trips acceptance + cancellation rate' shape, DoorDash's 'last-100-offers completion rate >= 90 percent' threshold, Convoy / Uber Freight's first-tender-acceptance signal, and Medely / Clipboard Health / CareRev / ShiftMed's 'shift fill rate + show-up rate' for clinician trust scoring. 2) Feed the dynamic-pricing model (per-(skill, zone) charge-rate recommendation in Medely, per-H3 surge multiplier in Uber, per-lane spot rate in Uber Freight, per-batch tip / pay incentive in DoorDash / Instacart) with sub-minute per-(skill x zone x product) rolling open-request count and available-supplier count so a learned or rules-based pricing controller can compute a supply-demand ratio and adjust the quote every few seconds. 3) Score per-customer / per-facility / per-shipper reliability (per-facility cancellation rate, per-shipper rate-to-market profile, per-restaurant prep-time velocity, per-warehouse load-wait time) so the marketplace can throttle low-quality demanders, surface higher prices to riskier customers, or filter offers to protect supplier-side experience and reduce no-show / cancellation churn. 4) Detect short-horizon supplier gaming (driver-side surge chasing, fake cancellations, no-shows by clinicians who claim shifts then no-show, repeated late acceptances at price-cap right before timeout) by computing per-supplier velocity / distribution features that the dispatcher reads on every offer.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Healthcare staffing (Medely / ShiftMed / CareRev / Clipboard / Nursa / IntelyCare) - shift_post {ts, facility_id, shift_id, role (RN/LVN/CNA/allied), skills[], specialty (ICU/ER/OR/Telemetry/L&D), credentials_required[], zip / h3, start_ts, end_ts, charge_rate}, professional_view {ts, professional_id, shift_id}, shift_apply / shift_book {ts, professional_id, shift_id, bid_rate}, shift_confirm, shift_cancel_by_pro {ts, professional_id, shift_id, hours_to_start, reason}, shift_cancel_by_facility {ts, facility_id, shift_id, hours_to_start, reason}, clock_in / clock_out, no_show {ts, professional_id, shift_id}, rating {ts, party, rating, role}. Delivery (DoorDash / Instacart / Uber Eats / Wolt / Rappi) - order_create {ts, order_id, store_id, h3, items[], total}, store_prep_event {ts, store_id, order_id, prep_seconds, queue_depth}, offer_create {ts, offer_id, dasher_id, order_id, eta_seconds, pay}, offer_response {ts, offer_id, accepted_or_declined, latency_ms}, batch_assignment {ts, dasher_id, order_ids[]}, pickup_event {ts, dasher_id, store_id, wait_at_store_s}, dropoff_event {ts, order_id, on_time_bool, actual_minus_predicted_s}. Freight (Uber Freight / Convoy / DAT / Loadsmart) - load_post {ts, load_id, origin_zip, dest_zip, equipment, weight, tender_lead_time_h, rate_cap}, carrier_state {ts, carrier_id, dot_id, lat_lng, equipment, available_capacity}, tender {ts, load_id, carrier_id, offered_rate}, tender_response {ts, accept_or_reject}, bid {ts, load_id, carrier_id, bid_rate}, pickup_event {ts, load_id, on_time_bool}, delivery_event {ts, load_id, on_time_bool, OS_and_D_bool}. Mobility (Uber, Lyft, Bolt, Didi, Grab, GoJek, inDriver) - ride_request {ts, rider_id, h3, product, origin, dest}, driver_state {ts, driver_id, h3, status}, offer {ts, offer_id, driver_id, request_id, eta_s, surge_mult}, offer_response {ts, accept_or_decline}, ride_cancel {ts, ride_id, canceller, hours_to_pickup}, ride_complete {ts, ride_id, eta_at_quote_s, actual_s}. All these naturally key on supplier_id, customer_id / facility_id / shipper_id, (skill_or_product x zone_or_h3 x time_bucket), (origin_zone x dest_zone x equipment_or_product), and (supplier_id x customer_id) collusion / repeat-relationship pairs - all directly expressible as @bv.table(key=...) composite keys.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Per-supplier (clinician / driver / dasher / carrier / contractor): rolling count(offer, last-100) and count(accept, last-100) -> acceptance_rate (Uber's published last-100 lookback window, DoorDash's last-100 offers, Lyft's mode-based stats); count(shift_book, 30d) and count(shift_completed, 30d) -> per-clinician fill_rate (the Medely / Clipboard Health / CareRev shift-fill metric); count(cancel_by_pro, 30d) and count(no_show, 90d) -> per-clinician reliability score; count(on_time_dropoff, 30d) -> per-dasher / per-carrier on_time_rate; velocity(complete, 1h / 24h) -> trips-per-hour / shifts-per-week supplier utilization; distance(price_offered vs lane_market_rate) for carriers (Uber Freight's rate-to-market predictor of FTA); distribution(rating, 30d) for star-rating drift detection. Per-(skill / product x zone / h3 x time bucket): sliding count(open_request, 1m / 5m / 30m) and count(available_supplier, 1m / 5m / 30m) over (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32) min Uber Gairos windows; derived supply_demand_ratio for surge / charge-rate updates every 30-60 s. Per-customer / per-facility / per-shipper: count(cancel_after_match, 30d) -> per-facility cancellation_rate; count(no_show_shift_by_facility, 90d); distribution(prep_seconds, 30d) -> per-restaurant prep-time velocity (DoorDash top-10 feature); distribution(load_wait_seconds, 90d) -> per-shipper / per-warehouse facility quality; count(tender_accepted_within_first_offer, 90d) -> first-tender-acceptance rate per shipper / lane (Uber Freight). Per-(supplier x customer) pair: count(repeat_book, 90d) -> the 'preferred clinician at facility X' or 'preferred carrier on lane Y' signal that all four verticals use to bias matching toward known-reliable pairs. All expressible as beava count / velocity / rate / distance / distribution primitives.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Heterogeneous and composite within one decision. Primary keys touched per decision: supplier_id (professional_id / driver_id / dasher_id / carrier_id / contractor_id), customer_id (facility_id / restaurant_id / shipper_id / rider_id), (skill_or_role x zone x time_bucket) for demand-supply counters (typically (role x zip3 x hour-of-day) in healthcare, (h3_cell_8 x product) in mobility, (origin_zip3 x dest_zip3 x equipment) for freight lanes), (supplier_id x customer_id) repeat-pair grain, shift_id / order_id / load_id / ride_id for transient per-request state. A single dispatch decision evaluates 5-50 candidate suppliers, each requiring per-supplier + per-zone + per-pair feature reads.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Predominantly sliding / hopping windows that align with public marketplace performance windows. Acceptance / cancellation rate: last-100 offers (Uber, DoorDash explicit) or last 30-90 days. Fill rate: 30-day rolling per clinician / dasher / carrier. No-show / late-cancel rate: 90-day rolling for healthcare (regulatory-visible at NLRB / Joint Commission level for staffing-firm certification). Demand-supply counters: (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32) min sliding for mobility surge (Uber Gairos public set), 1-15 min for delivery dispatch, sub-hour to multi-hour for freight tender lead time (typical Convoy tender lead times in hours). Approximate aggregates (HLL for n_unique(rider) per driver, n_unique(facility) per professional; CMS for top-K cancelling suppliers; T-Digest for ETA-error or prep-time distributions) are acceptable on the high-cardinality + ranking surfaces. Exact aggregates preferred on supply-demand ratios (a small error directly distorts a surge multiplier or charge-rate quote). Session-style windows useful for 'this driver just declined 5 offers in the last 10 min and went idle' supplier-state burst detection.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: At-least-once with idempotency-by-(event_id) is the de-facto industry standard for matching / pricing features. Surge multipliers, dispatch scores, charge-rate suggestions, and per-(skill,zone) counters can tolerate a small over-count (controllers re-evaluate every 30-60 s anyway and re-decisions wash out single duplicate events). Per-supplier acceptance / cancellation / fill-rate features are NOT regulator-grade in the online tier (warehouse audit copy is the regulator-grade record under EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 algorithmic-management evaluation obligations and Joint Commission Health Care Staffing Services Certification) but operators still want strong idempotency because these counters affect supplier livelihoods (deactivation, demotion to Standard Mode, removed from rewards tier - Uber's Advantage Mode and DoorDash's Top Dasher status both gate on these counters).

technical_fit.latency_budget: End-to-end matching budget is typically 100-500 ms (a few seconds is acceptable in healthcare because shifts are posted hours-to-days ahead; tens of ms on the inline driver-offer accept-or-decline ack in mobility). Per-feature read budget is single-digit ms - DoorDash dispatch optimizer needs to score thousands of (Dasher, order) pairs in a single MIP solve, Uber generates 30M+ match-pair predictions per minute. Aerospike-style feature stores publish 1-2 ms p95 with end-to-end ML pipelines at 20-100 ms in real production deployments. beava's published sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits inside the per-feature read budget for all four verticals.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Sub-minute on the supply-demand demand-supply ratio (Uber's surge recomputes every 30-60 s on H3 hexes, GoJek per minute on S2 L13 cells), seconds on the per-supplier offer-response and state-change features (a driver who just went offline must not be ranked highly on the next dispatch), seconds on prep-time / load-wait features (DoorDash's Order Ready Signal triggers immediate dispatch within seconds). For healthcare specifically, Medely's Chalk migration documented moving from '24-hour batch lag in Redis' to 'real-time at inference time' - i.e. shifts get matched in minutes, not the next day, and Medely cites 'verified professionals booked under 60 minutes even for high-demand roles' as the freshness target. beava's push-on-event no-broker model is at or below the Kafka -> Flink -> Redis pipeline freshness incumbents publish about, with no extra broker hop. [uncertain]
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Highly buyer-dependent and varies by vertical by ~3-4 orders of magnitude. Healthcare per-diem platforms (Medely 300k professionals, Clipboard Health tens of thousands of pros + 1k+ facilities, CareRev / ShiftMed / Nursa similar) operate in the 10-1,000 EPS range steady-state with peaks during shift-posting bursts - the throughput-limiting events are shift_post, view, apply, confirm, cancel, clock-in / clock-out, not high-frequency telemetry. Mid-market delivery / mobility (a regional ride-hail operator, a single-country delivery platform, a mid-market freight broker) is 1k-50k EPS. Tier-1 platforms (Uber, DoorDash, Lyft, Didi, Instacart, Uber Freight) are well past 100k EPS to 1M+ EPS aggregated - Uber globally serves ~10M ML predictions per second at peak, DoorDash processes 'hundreds of billions of events per day' (avg ~1-3M EPS), Convoy historically ran fully-automated brokering in 'top freight markets' with order-of-magnitude lower EPS than mobility. For Medely-class / Clipboard-class / mid-market-broker-class buyers, beava's published ~684k EPS comfortably fits within one node. Tier-1 aggregate EPS exceeds one beava box and requires partitioning that v0 does not ship. [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Read-leaning to balanced. Every match / dispatch / pricing decision triggers 5-50 candidate-supplier feature reads plus per-zone supply-demand counter reads plus per-customer reliability reads, while the write rate (supplier pings, offer events, state changes, completes, cancels) is also material. Net effect: 2:1 to 10:1 reads-per-write for healthcare and freight (lower write rate, decision-rich per request); closer to 1:1 for mobility / delivery once high-frequency driver location pings are included. Both regimes strongly favor beava's batch_get.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Healthcare: ~10^5-10^6 active professionals across a US-national platform, ~10^4 facilities, ~10^3 active (role x zip3 x hour-of-day) cells - dominated by professional + facility state at ~200-500 B per entity x ~80 active counter slots -> ~1-5 GB hot state for a Medely-class buyer; comfortably in one beava node. Delivery: ~10^6 active dashers + ~10^5 restaurants + ~10^6-10^7 listings + ~10^5-10^6 active H3 cells - ~5-20 GB regional hot state, in one beava node per region. Mobility (per region for a tier-1 operator): ~10^6 active drivers x ~200-500 B + ~10^4-10^6 H3 cells x 54 features = ~5-20 GB regional. Freight: ~10^5-10^6 active carriers / DOT-IDs + ~10^6 lanes (origin x dest x equipment) - smaller state, ~1-10 GB. Mid-market deployments across all four verticals fit one beava node; only tier-1 single-region (Uber-SF, DoorDash-NYC) blow past it. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Slowly-growing on supplier_id (signup-bounded; 10^5-10^7 globally), bounded on (skill x zone x time) cells (geographic + role-taxonomy bounded), explosive on the (supplier x customer) repeat-pair grain (long-tail, requires TTL eviction), slowly-growing on customer_id (facility_id / shipper_id / restaurant_id are bounded; rider_id explosive but typically counted via HLL). Lane / route cardinality (origin x dest x equipment x hour) is theoretically explosive but operators prune to top-K popular lanes (Uber Freight publishes lane-level pricing for popular lanes only). Much lower cardinality stress than ad-tech or IP-fraud surfaces.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Mixed and aligned with marketplace performance windows. Per-(zone x role) supply-demand windows: 1-32 min sliding; ephemeral. Per-supplier rolling acceptance / cancellation / completion rate: last-100 offers (Uber, DoorDash) or last 30-90 days. Per-clinician fill rate / no-show rate: 30-90 days. Per-(supplier x customer) repeat-pair counters: 90-180 days. Per-supplier long-term reputation: 12-24 months but materialized in the warehouse, not the online store. Per-lane / per-route rate-to-market and ETA-error history: weeks to months (slow-changing).
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 20-100 features per matching / pricing decision. Mobility / dispatch typically reads thousands of features in aggregate across all (rider, driver) pair scorers; per-pair vector is 20-50 features. Healthcare matching reads per-(professional, shift) pair vectors at 30-80 features (per-pro fill rate, per-pro acceptance, per-pro distance to facility, per-(pro, facility) history, per-(role, zone) demand). Freight tender-acceptance scoring is ~30-50 features. Strongly favors batch_get; canonical pattern is one batch_get per request for the per-decision feature vector.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Crash-safe rather than regulator-grade for the online tier. Per-(zone x role) windows are short (minutes) and can be replayed from the upstream event log within a couple of minutes. Per-supplier rolling acceptance / cancellation / fill rate is harder to replay (30-100 day windows) but operators tolerate a brief ~minutes warm-up after a node restart because (a) suppliers are still actively rolling new events in, (b) the gold-copy lives in the warehouse for EU Platform Work Directive Article 7-9 algorithmic-management impact assessments and Joint Commission staffing-firm certification audits. beava's WAL + periodic snapshot fits this tier. Cold-start replay time on a regional ~10-20 GB hot state is the open operational question. [uncertain]
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Single-binary regional / per-vertical sidecar is the dominant deployment shape. Healthcare staffing operates per-country (US-only for Medely / Clipboard / CareRev / ShiftMed / Nursa, EU-only for variants like Florence / Patchwork) so single-binary nation-scale is fully sufficient at the published ~684k EPS. Delivery and mobility are regional (Lyft's online feature store is regional). Freight brokerage is national + lane-keyed and fits single-binary nationally for all but Uber-Freight-scale carriers. Multi-region active-active not required (events are geo-local). beava v0's single-binary fit is actually a better match here than for global counter-consistency domains like ad-tech frequency capping. The hard v0 ceiling (no in-process sharding) bites only at tier-1 single-region scale (Uber-SF dispatch, DoorDash-NYC, Instacart-Bay-Area peak).

commercial_fit.who_buys: Marketplace / matching / pricing / ML platform engineering teams at: (a) on-demand healthcare staffing - Medely (publicly on Chalk), ShiftMed (W-2 model, AI-powered platform, on TODAY show), CareRev (acquired by IntelyCare Jan 2026), Clipboard Health (TechCrunch USD 80M raise 2022), Nursa, IntelyCare, ShiftKey (auction model), Trusted Health, Connect-RN, Florence (UK), Patchwork Health (UK / EU), Vivian Health; (b) on-demand delivery / convenience - DoorDash, Instacart, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Deliveroo, Wolt, Glovo, Rappi, Swiggy, Zomato, iFood, Gopuff and the q-commerce long tail (Getir, Flink, Blinkit, Zapp); (c) digital freight brokerage - DAT (acquired Convoy Platform July 2025 for ~USD 250M), Loadsmart, Uber Freight, Transfix, Cargomatic, Loadlink, J.B. Hunt 360, Truckstop; (d) ride / mobility - Uber, Lyft, Bolt, Didi, Grab, GoJek, Yandex Go, inDriver, Cabify, Curb, Free Now, Ola, plus the AV-rollout layer (Waymo, Cruise, Zoox) and micromobility (Lime, Bird); (e) services / blue-collar / gig adjacent - TaskRabbit, Thumbtack, Handy, Bluecrew, Wonolo, Snagajob's GoShifts, Veryable for manufacturing gig; (f) vendors who would embed beava as a feature backend - Chalk (already pitches Medely), Tecton (publishes ride-hailing demo), Fennel, Aerospike (Swiggy customer). Buyer persona is Marketplace Eng / Dispatch Eng / Pricing ML / ML Platform - not the operations / pricing-rules team above the feature layer.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Sum of four vertical TAMs adjacent to this use case is substantial. (1) Healthcare staffing - U.S. healthcare staffing market sized at USD 21-45B in 2025 across analysts, projected USD 33-90B by 2033-2035 at 5-9% CAGR; the per-diem nurse sub-segment specifically was USD 9.54B in 2024 -> USD 10.14B 2025 -> USD 13.59B by 2030 at 6.07% CAGR per Persistence Market Research; ~20% per-diem share of the broader staffing pie. (2) On-demand staffing platforms (SaaS / digital layer only) - USD 5-8B 2024-2025, projected USD 12-25B by 2033-2035 at 10-12% CAGR. (3) Digital freight brokerage / matching - USD 7.6B in 2025 (Fortune Business Insights) growing to USD 68.9B by 2034 at 27.7% CAGR; Marketresearch Future puts digital freight matching at USD 66B 2025 -> USD 1.087T by 2035 at 32% CAGR (an outlier); U.S. freight brokerage overall USD 19.7B 2025 -> USD 30.2B 2031. (4) Ride-hailing globally USD 47-182B 2025, food delivery roughly similar order. The infrastructure-layer slice (matching, pricing, feature serving) is the smaller silicon-layer share - order ~USD 5-25B across all four verticals in dedicated marketplace-infra spend, dominated today by in-house Kafka+Flink+Redis stacks plus commercial feature stores (Tecton, Chalk - Chalk has publicly pitched Medely cite ~USD 800k annual net-revenue lift on a single Chalk-powered charge-rate model). Public case-study capture by Chalk for Medely materially validates the 'per-supplier real-time feature serving' wedge in healthcare specifically. [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) EU Platform Work Directive (2024/2831, in force 1 Dec 2024, Member States transpose by 2 Dec 2026) explicitly requires algorithmic-management transparency, human oversight on dispatch / deactivation decisions, and bi-annual impact assessments of automated systems on gig workers - operators must be able to audit and explain what per-supplier features drive matching, which is operationally easier when the feature store has named primitives (count/velocity/rate) than when logic is buried in opaque Flink SQL. 2) Healthcare labor crisis and post-COVID nurse shortage - per-diem and gig nursing exploded; Medely's Chalk migration was driven by needing to go from 'daily batch features written to Redis (24-hour lag)' to real-time pricing/matching because 'jobs posted with as little lead time as 48 hours' (Chalk Medely case study). 3) IntelyCare's acquisition of CareRev in January 2026 plus general healthcare staffing consolidation increases pressure to differentiate on technology and supplier matching quality. 4) Joint Commission Health Care Staffing Services Certification is a procurement requirement for many hospitals - mandates documented competency, credential verification, and performance monitoring per professional, which maps onto per-supplier features beava can serve. 5) NLRB October 2023 joint-employer rule and W-2 vs 1099 misclassification risk (Uber for Nursing critique, March 2025 STAT report, Roosevelt Institute report) push staffing platforms toward W-2 models where per-supplier performance scoring becomes a managerial / supervisory decision needing rigorous justification. 6) Cost pressure post-2023 in delivery / mobility / freight - ride-hailing and delivery operators under shareholder pressure to reach contribution-margin profitability; replacing a multi-tier Kafka+Flink+Redis+DynamoDB matching stack with a single binary is directly accretive. 7) Convoy collapse (Oct 2023) and acquihires through July 2025 (Flexport sold the Convoy Platform to DAT for ~USD 250M) - the digital-freight tech vacuum has the second wave of brokers rebuilding matching stacks now. 8) Public engineering blog footprint - Uber Gairos / Marketplace Matching / Michelangelo / DeepETA, DoorDash DeepRed / Riviera, Lyft OSV reinforcement-learning matching ($30M+ incremental revenue / year cited in INFORMS paper), Instacart Griffin 2.0, Convoy's automated-brokering blog - has set expectations among mid-market engineering teams.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 - algorithmic-management transparency, human-oversight on dispatch / deactivation, biannual impact assessments on automated systems affecting platform workers, prohibition on processing emotional / psychological / trade-union / private-conversation data. EU AI Act (effective phases through 2025-2026) - classifies worker-management ML as high-risk in some readings, raising explainability requirements. GDPR / CCPA on supplier and customer PII (location, identity, ratings). NYC TLC and similar local regulators audit per-driver acceptance / cancellation / utilization rates for license enforcement. NLRB joint-employer rule (Oct 2023) - per-supplier features that bear on employment status must be auditable. Joint Commission Health Care Staffing Services Certification - documented competency / credential / performance monitoring per professional (the certification specifically measures placement and competency assessment processes at staffing firms). Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) on freight (SAFER / DOT-ID lookups, hours-of-service). State-level rideshare insurance and TNC rules (CA AB-5 reverberations). PCI-DSS on payouts. SOC 2 Type II is table stakes for any marketplace-buyer procurement. beava v0's lack of TLS / auth is a blocker for any production deployment outside a controlled VPC.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fast for the demo. A runnable per-clinician / per-driver acceptance + cancellation + fill rate + per-(role x zone) demand-supply demo on synthetic event data is a 1-3 day build - declare @bv.event for shift_post / shift_book / shift_cancel / no_show (or order_create / offer_response), @bv.table(key=professional_id) and @bv.table(key=(role, zip3)) and @bv.table(key=(professional_id, facility_id)) for the repeat-pair grain, seed events, batch_get. 2-6 weeks to a credible pilot at a mid-market healthcare-staffing or freight-broker buyer once TLS / auth / regional-deployment story is added. 3-9 months to displace a Kafka+Flink+Redis production stack at a regional mobility or delivery operator. Medely-Chalk-style headline 'replace batch Redis with real-time feature store' migration is the most directly comparable benchmark - Chalk reports Medely's ~USD 800k annual net-revenue lift on a single Chalk-powered charge-rate recommendation, plus collapsed experimentation cycles from ~2 months to 2-week sprints.

competition.incumbents: (a) In-house Kafka + Flink + Redis dominates at tier-1: Uber Gairos (Flink + Pinot + custom store; 30M+ match-pair predictions / min; H3 resolution 8), Uber Michelangelo / Palette (5k+ production models, 10M predictions / s at peak), Uber DeepETA, DoorDash DeepRed + Riviera (declarative Apache-Flink-based real-time feature framework), Lyft (Beam + Flink + DynamoDB + ValKey LRU; OSV online reinforcement learning for matching, INFORMS-paper $30M+ / year incremental revenue), Instacart Griffin 2.0 (Snowflake + Spark + Flink for batch + real-time, Feature Marketplace), Convoy's supply-availability score + dynamic pricing (AWS ML stack, fully-automated brokering in top markets). (b) Commercial feature stores - Tecton (publishes ride-hailing demo, ~USD 5 / credit list price), Chalk (publicly powers Medely's pricing + matching; also customer of Turo for vehicle search/pricing/risk), Fennel (AWS Marketplace, real-time + batch unified), Hopsworks, Feast (originated at GoJek). (c) Stream processors + serving stores - Flink, Spark Structured Streaming, Beam, RisingWave, Materialize plus Redis / Aerospike (Swiggy public customer, 1-2 ms p95) / DynamoDB / ScyllaDB / Dragonfly. (d) Geospatial-aware OLAP - Apache Pinot (Uber Gairos), Druid (Lyft), ClickHouse with H3 UDFs. beava's competitive surface is 'in-house Redis + Flink' for mid-market and 'Chalk / Tecton / Fennel' for greenfield buyers.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Healthcare staffing: Chalk is the publicly-named incumbent on real-time features (Medely case study); Snowflake + dbt + dashboard tooling is the older incumbent shape; IntelyCare and Aya Healthcare reportedly run more traditional staffing-firm stacks. Vendor matching engines (Bullhorn, Erecruit) are above the feature layer. Mobility: Uber's in-house Gairos / Michelangelo / DeepETA, Lyft's Beam-Flink-DynamoDB-ValKey stack, GoJek's Surbo (44k S2 L13 cells, ~1M data points/min peak) + Jaeger dispatch, Bolt / Grab / Didi internal. Delivery: DoorDash Riviera + DeepRed (Apache Flink declarative DSL, store-order-count and dasher-wait in top-10 ETA features), Instacart Griffin 2.0 (Feature Marketplace built atop Snowflake + Spark + Flink), Uber Eats on Uber's shared stack, Wolt / Deliveroo internal. Freight: Convoy's machine-learning matching + dynamic pricing on AWS (now operated by DAT), Uber Freight's dynamic-pricing algorithm (rate-to-market predictor of FTA), Loadsmart's TMS+brokerage stack, DAT's lane-rate analytics layer. Cross-vertical vendors with mobility / delivery demos: Tecton (ride-hailing demo in examples repo), Aerospike (Swiggy public deployment, feature-store positioning), Featureform / Hopsworks pitch dispatch use cases. No incumbent owns the 'single-binary regional matching + pricing feature server' niche beava could plausibly own.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary collapses (Kafka producer + Flink job + Redis / DynamoDB store + serving layer) into one process - the meaningful unlock for mid-market healthcare-staffing platforms (~10k-1k EPS), regional delivery / freight operators, and embedded vendors who don't want to operate a Kafka + Flink + Redis cluster per customer. 2) 50+ aggregation primitives natively express per-supplier acceptance / cancellation / fill / on-time / no-show rates, per-(skill,zone) supply-demand counters, per-(supplier,customer) repeat-pair counters, ETA-error / prep-time distributions - without writing Lua / Flink SQL / UDFs. The shape maps 1:1 to Uber's Gairos 54 features per H3 hex per minute pattern. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get is at parity with Aerospike (1-2 ms p95) and beats Redis-Lua + Flink-state-lookup chains - matches Uber/DoorDash/Lyft dispatch budgets. 4) Composite-key (pair / triple) aggregations natively support (supplier x customer), (skill x zone x time), (origin_zip x dest_zip x equipment) without hand-rolled hash-of-hash schemes - the load-bearing marketplace-matching signals. 5) Apache-2.0 with no open-core is attractive to (a) embedded use by Chalk / Tecton / Fennel competitors, (b) cost-conscious mid-market operators avoiding Tecton SaaS lock-in, and (c) staffing-tech vendors who don't want their feature serving infrastructure to be a competitor's managed cloud. 6) Push-on-event over HTTP/JSON :8080 and framed TCP :8081 fits dispatcher / pricing-controller event flows natively - shifts get posted, offers fire, accept-declines come back - no Kafka broker hop. 7) Per-key TTL + sliding-window semantics built-in means last-100-offer windows (Uber, DoorDash) and 30/60/90-day rolling rates need no custom Lua or stateful Flink operators. 8) The Medely-Chalk migration shape ('replace daily-batch Redis with real-time feature store at inference time') is a directly addressable pattern for beava - same job-to-be-done, no open-core SaaS dependency. 9) Healthcare-staffing platforms in the 'long tail below tier-1' (regional per-diem boards, vertical staffing for allied health, dental, EU labor-platforms under PWD 2024/2831) are nearly all greenfield on real-time features and represent low-friction adoption.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS / auth - disqualifying for any production deployment outside a tightly-controlled VPC; especially blocking in healthcare (HIPAA-adjacent ePHI sometimes flows alongside professional-id), in regulated platform-work jurisdictions (EU PWD requires authenticated logging of algorithmic-management decisions), and SOC 2 procurement. 2) No in-process sharding - tier-1 single-region dispatch (Uber-SF, DoorDash-NYC, Instacart-Bay-Area, Uber-Freight-national) blows past one beava node. 3) No geospatial index - H3 / S2 / geohash / zip3 cells are opaque composite keys; client must enumerate cells in a ring (typical Uber Gairos ring radius 0/1/2/3/4/5/10/15/20) and issue batch_get; Pinot / Druid push this server-side. 4) No triggers - dynamic-pricing and supplier-deactivation flows need 'fire when per-(zone) supply_demand_ratio crosses 1.2' or 'fire when per-pro 30d_no_show_rate > threshold' callbacks; today these must be polled. 5) No multi-tenancy primitives - vendors serving many staffing customers / many delivery operators on shared infrastructure need per-tenant namespaces, quotas, rate-limit accounting. 6) No secondary indexes - 'top-K low-acceptance drivers' or 'top-K facilities with high cancellation' analyst surfaces require materializing the keyspace; Uber / DoorDash dashboards expose this today. 7) No native PII / right-to-erasure cascade for GDPR Art. 17 / EU PWD worker-data deletion across all derived per-supplier aggregates. 8) No public marketplace / dispatch case study or demo in the repo yet - python/beava/demos/ contains adtech, ecommerce, fraud only; no matching / pricing / staffing demo. [uncertain] 9) Cold-start replay time on a regional ~5-20 GB hot state is unbenchmarked publicly. [uncertain] 10) No regulator-grade durability tier for PWD biannual impact assessments or Joint Commission audit retention - that's an upstream warehouse job, but the seam needs documenting. 11) No native financial-ledger integration for charge-rate / bill-rate reconciliation (Medely-style charge-rate recommendations decide money; ground truth lives in the ledger, not in beava counters). 12) No native fairness / disparate-impact monitoring under EU AI Act high-risk-AI requirements for worker matching.
competition.integration_surface: Producers: marketplace app backend (shift-post / order-create / load-tender / ride-request via HTTP/JSON :8080), supplier app (offer-response, location-ping, clock-in/out via framed TCP :8081 to absorb high write rate), dispatcher / matching service (offer-create, batch-assignment via gRPC or TCP wrapped to beava), ratings / completion / cancel service (HTTP), credential-verification / background-check webhook for healthcare (Sumsub / Persona / Onfido / Universal Background Screening), payment processor for charge-rate / bill-rate reconciliation (Stripe Connect, Adyen, Marqeta for ICs), TMS for freight (McLeod, MercuryGate, MyCarrierPackets). Consumers: matching engine / dispatcher (batch_get per request), dynamic-pricing controller (polling per-zone features every 30-60 s), per-supplier scoring service (XGBoost / LightGBM, ONNX-runtime sidecar), supplier-reliability / deactivation workflow (rules engine + ML score), inline ranking ML in the app gateway. beava's HTTP+TCP push surface fits an event-driven marketplace better than a Kafka-only feature store (Feast) that requires running Kafka + connectors; mid-market operators in healthcare / freight typically don't have a Kafka backbone and beava lets them skip standing one up.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Rules engines (Joint Commission credentialing thresholds, NLRB joint-employer thresholds, per-zone surge multiplier rules, supplier-suspension thresholds like 'last-100 acceptance < 50% AND last-100 cancellation > 10% then demote to Standard Mode' a la Uber Advantage Mode) coexist with ML scorers (Medely's charge-rate model, DoorDash DeepRed MIP solver fed by ML predictions, Uber's 30M match-pair-predictions / min ensemble of tree-based + ensembling, Lyft OSV online reinforcement learning for matching, Convoy supply-availability score). beava sits below all of them as the feature backend; both rules and ML read the same batch_get.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public beava users on this domain yet. [uncertain] Direct comparable case study: Chalk x Medely - publicly documented healthcare-staffing real-time-matching deployment that explicitly replaced 'daily batch features written to Redis (24-hour lag)' with real-time feature serving at inference time, projected ~USD 800k annual net-revenue lift on a single Chalk-powered charge-rate model alone, experimentation cycles compressed from ~2 months to 2-week sprints. Other comparable production systems with heavy public documentation: Uber Marketplace Matching (30M+ match-pair predictions / min, thousands of features per pair, H3 res-8 surge), Uber Michelangelo / Palette (5k+ production models, 10M predictions / s peak), Uber DeepETA (single-digit ms p99 at hundreds-of-thousands QPS), Uber Freight (rate-to-market predicts FTA, ML auto-negotiation, 1.7M+ drivers), Lyft OSV reinforcement-learning matching (USD 30M+ / year incremental revenue, INFORMS paper), DoorDash DeepRed (MIP optimization, ML-predicted acceptance probability, store-order-count and dasher-wait in top-10 ETA features), DoorDash Riviera (Apache Flink declarative real-time feature framework), Instacart Griffin 2.0 (Feature Marketplace bridging Snowflake / Spark / Flink), Convoy's automated brokering + supply-availability score on AWS (now operated by DAT), Aerospike + Swiggy (1-2 ms p95 feature store). On the staffing-platform side: Medely's Talent Fusion (Chalk-powered), ShiftMed (AI-powered platform, W-2 model), CareRev (acquired by IntelyCare Jan 2026), Clipboard Health (USD 80M Sequoia Series C Apr 2022), Nursa, ShiftKey (auction model). Adjacent: Tecton examples repo includes a ride-hailing-style streaming demo.
adoption_signals.community_discussions: No beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion / RFC threads on marketplace matching / pricing identified in this snapshot. [uncertain] Adjacent communities are extremely active: Uber Engineering blog series on Marketplace Matching, Gairos, DeepETA, surge pricing, H3 (h3geo.org / github.com/uber/h3 is active OSS, MIT-licensed), Michelangelo, Palette; DoorDash Engineering blog (DeepRed, Riviera, declarative feature engineering); Lyft Engineering blog + p99 conf talks on online feature serving; Instacart 'How It's Made' blog (Griffin 2.0); Convoy engineering posts on supply-availability score and pricing ML (now archived under DAT); Apache Flink / Beam / Pinot / Druid community channels; FeatureStore.org community; Chalk customers page; Tecton blog; arXiv mobility / pricing / dispatch papers including the Lyft OSV INFORMS publication; Roosevelt Institute / King's College London / STAT / AlgorithmWatch / LPE Project critiques of 'Uber for Nursing' algorithmic management (March 2025).
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: No marketplace-matching / dispatch / staffing demo in /python/beava/demos/ as of the snapshot - existing demos are adtech, ecommerce, fraud only (verified by ls at /tmp/docker-desktop-root/run/desktop/mnt/host/d/Code/Beava/beava/python/beava/demos/). A natural addition would be /python/beava/demos/marketplace_matching with @bv.event for shift_post / shift_book / shift_cancel / no_show / offer_response and @bv.table aggregations keyed by professional_id / dasher_id / carrier_id, (role x zip3) / (h3 x product) / (origin x dest x equipment), and (supplier_id x customer_id) - 1-3 day authoring effort. [uncertain] This is a gap to fill before pitching healthcare-staffing, freight or mobility buyers; given the Chalk x Medely case study is the most directly comparable public reference, a beava 'Medely-clone' demo is unusually high-leverage.
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Low to moderate. Suppliers (drivers, dashers, clinicians, carriers) occasionally game incentives - surge-chasing, position-spoofing, fake cancellations right before timeout, clinicians no-showing after grabbing a shift, drivers gaming acceptance-rate thresholds to stay in Advantage Mode / Top Dasher status. The CNBC / Roosevelt / King's College London critique-cycle on 'Uber for Nursing' surfaced concerns about clinician gaming and platform algorithmic asymmetry. But the headline domain is not adversary-driven the way fraud / bot defence / payments fraud is - feature drift is slower, threats are operational scale rather than active-attack. Adversarial signal lives mostly in the per-supplier acceptance / cancellation / no-show features themselves, which double as both a quality signal and a gaming-detection signal.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Historical lookback for offline training of pricing / matching models - that's a lakehouse / Parquet / Snowflake job (Hudi / Iceberg / Delta), not beava. beava feeds online inference, not training. 2) Geospatial joins ('all drivers within 2 km of cell X', 'all clinicians within 30 miles of facility Y') - beava has no geospatial index; the caller enumerates cells client-side (uber/h3 library) and issues batch_get; server-side ring / radius queries belong in Pinot / Druid / ClickHouse-with-H3-UDFs. 3) The dispatch optimizer / MIP solver itself - beava is the feature backend underneath DeepRed / Hungarian-matching / OSV-RL / Uber Freight pricing, not the optimizer. 4) Multi-region active-active counter consistency - not actually required for mobility / delivery / freight / staffing (events are geo-local) so this is a non-issue rather than a gap. 5) Acting as system of record for supplier / customer identity, payouts, ratings, credentials - those live in OLTP / data-warehouse upstream. 6) Long-retention regulator audits (EU PWD biannual impact assessments, Joint Commission audit history, NYC TLC per-driver audits) - those live in the warehouse / lakehouse. 7) Generative-AI / LLM context features (Michelangelo's 2024+ generative push, DoorDash's AI customer-service assistants) - beava is for tabular streaming features, not LLM context. 8) Cross-entity OLAP joins ('top-100 H3 cells by demand for UberX across all cities last hour', 'top-K facilities by 30-day cancellation rate') - that's a Pinot / Druid / OLAP query. 9) Image / NLP classification on shift descriptions, resumes, listing images - beava counts hashes / digests, doesn't compute them. 10) Charge-rate / spot-rate / payout reconciliation against the financial ledger - beava's counters drive recommendations; the ledger is the source of truth. 11) Fairness / disparate-impact monitoring under EU AI Act for worker matching - belongs in a separate audit subsystem on the warehouse copy.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava needs to ship to be production-grade for matching + pricing, in rough priority order: 1) TLS termination + token / mTLS auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 - single biggest gap, blocks healthcare-staffing (HIPAA-adjacent), platform-work jurisdictions (EU PWD logging requirements), SOC 2 procurement. 2) Triggers / 'fire callback when (zone).supply_demand_ratio crosses K' or 'when (supplier).30d_no_show_rate crosses K' - dynamic pricing and supplier-deactivation are inherently threshold-driven; polling 10k-10^7 keys every 30s is wasteful. 3) First-class composite-key (pair / triple) aggregations - (supplier_id, customer_id), (skill_or_product, zone, time_bucket), (origin_zone, dest_zone, equipment), (supplier_id, last-100-offers) - need ergonomic @bv.table key syntax. 4) Geospatial / H3 / S2 / geohash / zip3 key helpers and a documented client recipe for ring / radius batch_get using uber/h3 (no server-side geospatial index, but a worked example removes adoption friction). 5) HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K as first-class aggregations - bounded per-supplier unique-customer counters during peak load, bounded per-zone unique-supplier counters, top-K low-acceptance suppliers for analyst review. If already in the 50+ primitives, surface them prominently in a marketplace demo. 6) In-process or sidecar sharding by key prefix for tier-1 single-region scale. 7) Per-key TTL / sliding-window eviction aligned with last-100-offer windows (Uber, DoorDash) and 30/60/90-day rolling rates so supplier and pair cardinality stays bounded. 8) Multi-tenancy primitives (per-tenant namespaces, quotas, rate-limit accounting) so Chalk-competitor vendors can embed beava per-customer. 9) Streaming admin / debug surface + secondary indexes so analysts can run 'top-K suppliers by last-100 cancellation rate' or 'top-K zones by supply-demand ratio right now' without materializing the full keyspace. 10) PII handling: supplier_id / location / payout hashing at rest, configurable retention, right-to-erasure cascades through all derived aggregates (GDPR Art. 17, EU PWD worker-data deletion). 11) A vertical demo in /python/beava/demos/marketplace_matching covering (a) per-supplier acceptance / cancellation / on-time rate over last-100-offer windows, (b) per-(role x zone) demand-supply counters over 1/2/4/8/16/32 min windows, (c) per-(supplier x customer) repeat-pair counters, (d) per-customer reliability counters - this is the single most adoption-accelerating artifact missing today. 12) Documented seam between online-tier (beava) and audit-tier (warehouse) for EU PWD biannual impact assessments and Joint Commission staffing-firm certification. 13) Documented charge-rate-recommendation reference architecture (sidecar XGBoost / LightGBM reading per-(role x zip3 x hour) demand-supply features + per-pro fill rate + per-facility cancellation rate) modeled on the Medely-Chalk public pattern. 14) Cold-start WAL replay benchmark for ~5-20 GB regional hot state. 15) Optional Kafka / Kinesis fan-in shim for operators (DoorDash, Uber, large delivery / freight) who already run Kafka and want beava alongside, not instead of.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes - strongly. Dynamic pricing is fundamentally threshold-crossing ('when (zone).supply_demand_ratio crosses 1.2, raise charge rate'; 'when first-tender-acceptance for lane X drops below threshold, raise spot rate'; 'when (role x zip).open_shifts vs available_pros crosses K, raise charge-rate recommendation to facility'). Supplier-quality enforcement is the same shape ('when (driver).last-100-cancellation > 10% AND last-100-acceptance < 50%, demote to Standard Mode'; 'when (professional).30d_no_show_rate > threshold, escalate to manual review'; 'when (carrier).last-50-FTA < 60%, throttle inbound tenders'). Today operators poll - per-zone features every 30-60 s, per-supplier features on every offer - which works for the matching path (read happens anyway) but is wasteful and high-latency for the deactivation / pricing-update / supplier-friction path. First-class triggers are one of the two highest-priority gaps along with TLS + auth.
